proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived supported full-record lower certificates, observable upper bounds, an evaluated subexponential matched window, and an exact consistency criterion; the final mathematical panel passed after all six sources were attested. The promised uniform all-(b,d) constant-factor frontier and globally attaining estimator were not delivered: the critical exponential band and large-sample onset remain open, with a d^(3/2) gap between current envelopes. No Lean formalization was performed; bank downgraded at incremental under the standing field-floor decision, with retry permitted only for genuinely new mathematics.
tldr: Lower-tail rollout evaluation requires more than a mean treatment effect. This proposal studies the change in shortfall below the public cutoff one half in a single fair source-randomized experiment with bounded heterogeneous affine responses and disjoint interference blocks. The focal object is the uniformly evaluated minimax precision function \(r(b,d)\), together with an observable attaining procedure and a complete-record converse. Existing internal subcritical and eventual calculations are boundary evidence; the critical transition and uniform large-sample onset are the open mathematical content. The economic consumer is the public-cutoff shortfall component of a rollout lower-tail risk calculation, rather than the optimized CVaR functional.
gap: Available low-order numerical mean scores and low-order conditional-CDF scores concern different response restrictions. The occupied shortfall calculations leave an interval between their sample regimes and do not certify a uniform onset at the boundary base.
fill: An evaluated all-\((b,d)\) risk theorem, with a total procedure and legal full-table testing certificates, determines the precision cost of a public-cutoff downside benchmark without adding a coefficient distribution or a margin condition.
